ca_fortress_the_7.blurb: A compact trad crag in the Wonderland section of Joshua Tree National Park, one of the formations grouped under Grey Giant. The cliff is a long spine running east to west, and its north side is cut by many crack systems of differing angles, with a little face climbing mixed in. Twelve trad lines range from 5.9 to the low 5.12s, bunched mostly around 5.10 with a few at 5.11. Carry a full rack with cams to about 4 inches, and two ropes for the rappels. The walk in is among the longer ones in the park and includes sand wash, scrambling and boulder hopping.

ca_gettin_western_corridor.blurb: A short sport wall in the Alabama Hills outside Lone Pine, in the Eastern Sierra. It is the middle one of the north-south rock blades called the Corridors, which line the right-hand side as you enter Cattle Pocket. All twelve routes are bolted. Most sit in the 5.10 range, with a few easier lines from 5.7 to 5.9 and a handful of 5.11s, so it suits climbers working up into the 5.10s. The neighboring corridors are right alongside, which makes it simple to string several walls together in a day.

ca_hatchery_the.blurb: A big conglomerate formation in Texas Canyon, a high-desert sport area in the Angeles National Forest between Santa Clarita and Agua Dulce. It forms the west side of the First Corridor, and lines are found on all four sides. Of the twelve climbs, eleven are bolted sport routes and one is trad, running from 5.6 to 5.12 with a cluster around 5.10 and another near 5.12. Expect pockets, knobs and cobbles. Some bases need a scramble, and a second rope helps for reaching the top anchors. The rock is brittle and holds can snap off, so let it dry fully before touching it.

ca_island_wall.blurb: A small bouldering and top-rope wall at the southern end of Mount Rubidoux above Riverside, within the Island Area, a cluster of rocks that looks like an island when viewed from the main summit. The wall faces southeast and stands taller than the boulders around it. Twelve climbs are listed: mostly boulder problems from V1 up to V7, plus a few top-rope lines between 5.6 and 5.10. Part of the formation sits beside an old road and the rest on the hillside, so the walk from the car is brief. Broken glass has been reported at the base.

ca_java_wall.blurb: The busiest wall at Echo Cliffs, a bolted sport crag in the Santa Monica Mountains of the Los Angeles area. It makes up the right side of the large open-book corner you can see from the trail on the way in, and it is shaded in the morning. Twelve sport routes and linkups: one easy line, then four at 5.11, six at 5.12 and one at 5.13. Many lines are long, so a 60 m rope is useful. Echo Cliffs is most comfortable in fall, winter and spring, though summer climbing is possible. Expect a hike of roughly 40 to 60 minutes.

ca_lava_dome.blurb: A dark, jagged formation that closes off the Towers of Uncertainty to the south, in Joshua Tree's Queen Valley. Rather than a rounded dome it is steep and craggy: the north side shows three obvious cracks and the west face is fairly smooth. Of the twelve routes, nine are trad, two are top-rope and one is bolted. Grades climb from 5.4 through 5.11, with four in the 5.10 range, so both newer and stronger climbers find something. The approach is a sandy wash walk past other formations from the Crow's Nest and Reef Rock side.
